title: Transported graded Leibniz recurrence for canonical square-zero tensor boundaries
statement: Let j:Z -> X be a closed immersion of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion], L an invertible module [def-sc-invertible-module], I=j.ker [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], and I^2=0 [def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers]. Use tensor pullback and its canonical adjunction [def-pc-module-pullback, lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction]. Assume the derived-category instances needed for the canonical section boundaries [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, lem-sc-module-section-boundary-exact], and assume every degree-d canonical unit kernel sequence is short exact. For n>=0 and a global section s of N=(j^*L)^n, put F=j^*(I tensor L^n), H=H^1(Z,-) [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology], and f=homOfGlobalSection N s. There exist isomorphisms a_e:j^*(L^(n(e+1))) -> N^(e+1), additive equivalences b_e:H(F tensor N^e) -> H^1(X,kernel(unit_(n(e+1)))), and classes c_e in H(F tensor N^e), for every e>=0. The canonical boundary of (tensorPowSection f (e+1); a_e^-1)(1) is b_e(c_e). Moreover c_(e+1)=H(mulTensorPowSection f F e 1)(c_e)+H(rho_F^-1; id_F tensor tensorPowSection f (e+1))(H(rho_F)(c_0)). Here mulTensorPowSection multiplies the N^e factor by s, and rho_F:F tensor O_Z -> F is the right unitor. No closed exponent formula is asserted.

source.place: Tag 09MS, equation (30.17.5.1) and the direct-sum exact sequence and derivation calculation following it; https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09MS; Tag 0B8S, https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0B8S

proof.text: Tensor the closed-immersion ideal sequence with each invertible L^d. The multiplication inclusion identifies I tensor L^d with the categorical kernel of the canonical tensor-pullback unit, and the unit-quotient theorem supplies its quotient. Compare tensor pullback and Mathlib pullback by uniqueness of left adjoints, and use their tensor-power comparisons and tensorPowMulIso to obtain the degree comparisons a_e. Include degree zero throughout.

The ideal-tensor kernels are quasi-coherent and annihilated by I because I^2=0. The annihilated-module unit identifies each kernel with the pushforward of its pullback. The affine-morphism cohomology edge and the generic module-pullback tensor comparison (applied to the ideal-tensor module, which need not be invertible) identify the degree n(e+1) kernel cohomology with H^1(Z,F tensor N^e). Let b_e be the inverse additive equivalence, and let c_e be the inverse image under b_e of the canonical boundary of the section s^(e+1) transported by a_e; hence boundary_e=b_e(c_e). This determines c_e uniquely.

Sum the ideal sequences in all nonnegative tensor degrees. Local frames identify the middle graded algebra with a polynomial algebra; thus it and the quotient are commutative. The summed kernel is square zero since each product has two ideal factors. Apply the square-zero boundary derivation theorem to s times s^(e+1), without inducting on e. Include and project graded summands to identify the degree n(e+2) boundary. Naturality transports its first term to H^1(mulTensorPowSection f F e 1)(c_e) and its second to H^1(rho_F^-1; id_F tensor tensorPowSection f (e+1))(H^1(rho_F)(c_0)). The degree-zero right unitor identifies F tensor N^0 with F. Comparison of resolution boundaries with the canonical triangle boundary gives precisely the displayed recurrence.

lean.statement: theorem exists_square_zero_tensor_boundary_leibniz {X Z : Scheme.{u}} (j : Z ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion j] [HasDerivedCategory.{wC} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))] [HasDerivedCategory.{wD} (ModuleCat.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).obj.obj (Opposite.op ⊤)))] (L : X.Modules) [L.IsInvertible] (hI : j.ker ^ 2 = ⊥) (n : ℕ) (s : (((tensorPullback j).obj L).tensorPow n).val.presheaf.obj (Opposite.op ⊤)) (hshort : ∀ d : ℕ, (ShortComplex.kernelSequence ((Classical.choose (exists_tensorPullbackAdjunction j)).unit.app (L.tensorPow d))).ShortExact) : let F : Z.Modules := (tensorPullback j).obj (j.ker.toModules ⊗ L.tensorPow n) let N : Z.Modules := ((tensorPullback j).obj L).tensorPow n let H := RingedSpace.moduleCohomology Z.toRingedSpace 1 let f := homOfGlobalSection N s ∃ a : ∀ e : ℕ, (tensorPullback j).obj (L.tensorPow (n * (e + 1))) ≅ N.tensorPow (e + 1), ∃ b : ∀ e : ℕ, H.obj (show Z.Modules from F ⊗ N.tensorPow e) ≃+ (RingedSpace.moduleCohomology X.toRingedSpace 1).obj (kernel ((Classical.choose (exists_tensorPullbackAdjunction j)).unit.app (L.tensorPow (n * (e + 1))))), ∃ c : ∀ e : ℕ, H.obj (show Z.Modules from F ⊗ N.tensorPow e), (∀ e : ℕ, RingedSpace.moduleSectionBoundary X.toRingedSpace (ShortComplex.kernelSequence ((Classical.choose (exists_tensorPullbackAdjunction j)).unit.app (L.tensorPow (n * (e + 1))))) (hshort (n * (e + 1))) ((tensorPowSection f (e + 1) ≫ (a e).inv).app ⊤ (1 : Γ(Z, ⊤))) = b e (c e)) ∧ ∀ e : ℕ, c (e + 1) = H.map (mulTensorPowSection f F e 1) (c e) + H.map ((ρ_ F).inv ≫ F ◁ tensorPowSection f (e + 1)) (H.map (ρ_ F).hom (c 0))
